newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Eltin ends Leyshon contract,resumes Refugio.
newsitem.headline: Eltin ends Leyshon contract,resumes Refugio.

text.p: Mining contractor Eltin Ltd said on Wednesday agreement had been reached for the early termination of its Mt Leyshon contract in Queensland and access had been re-established to the Refugio mine site in Chile.
Eltin said mutual agreement had been reached with Mt Leyshon Gold Mines Ltd to end the Mt Leyshon contract seven months ahead of schedule on August 31, 1997.

Earlier this month Eltin said it expected net profit before abnormals for the 1996/97 second half to be similar to that of the first half - lower than previously expected - after problems with contracts in Chile and Australia.

It said then the performance of the Mt Leyshon contract had deteriorated in the last four months and the A$4 million provision raised last year would not be enough to cover expected losses which would hit 1996/97 earnings.
Eltin's managing director Nick Bowen said in a statement the Mt Leyshon contract would now be completed within the A$2 million provision for contract losses made for the 1997/98 year.
Eltin said mining operations at Refugio, which had been closed since June 10 after abnormally heavy snowfalls, had recommenced.

Also in the statement, Bowen said that while the company was concerned about the longer-term impact for the gold industry of current levels of the gold price, it did not foresee any problems in the short or medium term for Eltin.
Sixty-five percent of the company's current work on hand related to gold mining, he said.

However Eltin's clients had an average cash operating cost of about A$325 per ounce and the majority had significant forward sales contracts covering production beyond existing contractual terms, he said.
In the 1996/97 first half to end-December, Eltin posted a net profit of A$6.33 million after an abnormal profit of A$230,000.
